Workshop 1: AI-Ready for Your Career — Turning Fear into Opportunity. Speaker: Prisca Onyebuchi. June 01, 2026, 12:00 PM. Online (virtual). 60 minutes. Most women in 2026 are doing one of two things with AI. Either they are avoiding it entirely because they have decided it is for "technical people," or they are downloading every new tool, collecting screenshots of prompt frameworks, and quietly drowning in a stack of ten apps they barely use. Both moves come from the same place. Both moves keep you exactly where you are.

The women who will actually pull ahead this decade are not the ones with the longest tool stack or the most certifications. They are the ones who pick one AI tool, go deep, and use it to solve a problem that is theirs. Not the market's. Not their boss's. Theirs. The skill that wins is not coding. It is knowing what good looks like in your own domain, and AI cannot take that from you because you already have it.

In this session, Prisca Onyebuchi, a Black woman who taught herself AI development on top of a Computer Science degree and now builds custom AI solutions for premium clients, gives you the operator's lens on your own career. You will hear the story of the night her bank account got loud enough to drown the shame of being scared. You will get a three-question framework you can use the same afternoon. And you will leave with one experiment to run this week, on one problem that is yours, with one tool you actually understand.

This is not a workshop about which AI tools to learn. It is not a career-strategy framework or a learning roadmap. It is the conversation that has to happen before any of those become useful. The conversation about who you decide to be in a decade where every job is being rewritten, and the only sin is looking away.

Workshop 2: From AI-Assisted to AI-Native — Career Strategy. Speaker: Farshad Rouhani. June 02, 2026, 4:00 PM. Online (virtual). 60 minutes. The shift from using AI as a tool to working inside AI-native systems is the defining workforce transition of the decade.
In this session, we'll trace the adoption arc organizations are moving along, from efficiency wins to fundamental redesign,
and unpack what it means for the people inside those organizations or joining them. Expect a clear-eyed look at how
industries are evolving with AI, plus a framework for positioning yourself for durable employability rather than short-term advantage.

Workshop 3: The Experimentation Habit — The Skill That Future-Proofs You. Speaker: Ysimer (Ysi) Gonzalez. June 03, 2026, 4:00 PM. Online (virtual). 60 minutes. Everyone’s talking about AI. Most people are using it to do the same thing they’ve always done: just faster. That’s not a strategy. That’s duct tape.
The professionals who will actually pull ahead are the ones who develop the habit underneath the tool: the ability to observe how they work,
test small changes, learn from the results, and build something repeatable. That habit is what makes AI useful.
Without it, you’re just prompting into the void.
In this session, Ysi —founder of Vantelira Inc. and former Fortune 500 supply chain leader — gives you the operator’s lens, applied to your own career.
You’ll learn how to map what you’re already doing, run small experiments on the parts that matter most,
and turn what works into a repeatable process that AI can actually support.
This isn’t a job search tutorial. It’s the thinking skill that makes every next tool and every next career move easier to navigate.

Workshop 4: Agility and AI Literacy — A Non-Linear Learning Path. Speaker: Marie-Claire Asseko. June 04, 2026, 4:00 PM. Online (virtual). 60 minutes. Forget the "AI certification" trap. In a world where 39% of core skills will shift by 2030, AI literacy isn't a destination you reach:
It's a non-linear journey of constant adaptation. All of us have to move beyond being "AI-curious" to becoming "AI-agile."
In this session, we will dive deep into adopting a high-agency mindset and shifting from being a "maker" to a "manager of agents".
You’ll learn how to treat obstacles as simple "skill issues," develop a high-value "skill of rejection" to reinforce your Human Advantage,
and how "vibe coding" can help you bypass technical gaps. Stop waiting for an organizational roadmap and learn how to build your
own development plan through the power of active experimentation and extreme agency!

Workshop 5: From Employee to Architect — Portfolio Career in the Age of AI. Speaker: Natalie Loop. June 05, 2026, 4:00 PM. Online (virtual). 60 minutes. The career ladder is dead — and that's actually good news for women.
The future of work isn't a single title, a stable job description, or a linear climb. It's a portfolio. It's fractional. It's fluid.
And women — with their inherent adaptability, relational intelligence, and multi-dimensional skill sets — are uniquely positioned to thrive in it.
Yet too many women are still applying for one role, waiting to feel "ready enough," and defaulting to employee mode when they could be designing something entirely their own.
In this workshop, Natalie Loop — Founder & CEO of Alygra and fractional HR strategist for AI-era startups — shares what she's observed working alongside founders, operators,
and people leaders across Canada and Europe: women have extraordinary ideas and capabilities, but a reflex gap is holding them back.
We'll explore:
Why the entrepreneurial reflex comes slower to women — and how to rewire it
What a "portfolio career" actually looks like in practice (founder + fractional + employee — all at once)
How AI is accelerating new work formats and what that unlocks specifically for women
Practical steps to start designing your career like a CEO, not a candidate
